cases.name: Crossing without a junction
cases.description: Two complete strokes cross in the declared affine support. They have four endpoint sites and two physical components. Both proposed depth orders remain unresolved; neither creates a shared site.

cases.name: One actual four-arm junction
cases.description: The same visible support is split into four strokes meeting at one actual shared site. A connection query sees one component and six incident stroke pairs. The projected-crossing reader need not invent an extra intersection.

cases.name: Actual branching Y
cases.description: Three strokes share a site with no opposed ray pair. This is actual branching topology; its Y-like read does not claim historical growth, botanical identity, or ownership by one original object.

cases.name: Actual T junction
cases.description: One shared site has three incident rays, including one opposed pair. The branch is known; an absorbing or transmitting flow law would still need a separate connection contract.

cases.name: A stem merely reaches the rail
cases.description: The picture agrees with the T, but the rail has no middle site and the stem endpoint remains independent. Formal contact support is evidence for a possible reading, not authority to split the rail or weld sites.

cases.name: Gap with an apparent overpass
cases.description: Facing collinear endpoints support a proposed continuation. A separate transverse strand occupies the gap, supporting an occlusion hypothesis. Deliberate cut endpoints remain a competing candidate; no hidden line is asserted.

cases.name: Offset gap refuses collinear completion
cases.description: The separated horizontal strands are offset in the other axis. The blocked witness retains that displacement; a same-direction impression cannot establish a straight hidden continuation.

cases.name: Angular crossing remains open
cases.description: Both strokes carry two-axis displacement. This narrow reader deliberately supplies no general angular-intersection solver. The source is complete while that selected question remains open.

limits: Sources are authored native stroke observations, not parsed photographs or generated-recipe metadata.
Shared sites, formal projected intersections, continuation proposals, depth-order proposals and legal material transfer are separate reads.
The projected-intersection reader is bounded to declared axis-aligned intervals. Unsupported angular intersections and unresolved formal orders remain open.
Every continuation or depth proposal retains open obligations. No candidate installs a junction or modifies the observed source.
Component counts under a continuation proposal describe an observational grouping, not accepted physical connectivity or a transfer route.
T/Y/X/L summaries are native ray-incidence descriptions. L does not establish a right angle, and T does not establish absorption.
Screen angles, equal illustrative lengths, line weight and colour are renderer choices. They are not input to the inference reader.
Glyph recognition, inferred object ancestry, automatic junction commitment, learned salience and general weave reconstruction remain untested.
